Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, was founded in 1735 by the French governor Bertrand-François Mahé de La Bourdonnais as the main harbour of the colony then called Isle de France.

France had taken the island after the Dutch left. La Bourdonnais built docks, roads, forts and sugar works, using enslaved people from Madagascar and East Africa. The port became the French base in the Indian Ocean, from which fleets and privateers attacked British ships bound for India.

That made it a target. Britain took the island in 1810 after the Battle of Grand Port. Under British rule Port Louis was the landing place of the indentured labourers from India and the sugar port, and it is now a busy financial centre.
sum: Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, was founded in 1735 by the French governor Bertrand-François Mahé de La Bourdonnais as the main harbour of the colony then called Isle de France.
